Gaurav Singh, learned  as well as learned A.G.A.
and perused the record.

Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn
my attention to the post mortem report which
reveals the cause of death as Asphyxia due to
ante mortem hanging and apart from ligature
mark, no other injury was found on the body of the
deceased. It is thus argued that it is case of
suicidal death and there is no material to
substantiate that the applicant has subjected the
deceased to any physical or mental harassment in
relation to demand of dowry.  Hence, the applicant
being husband of the deceased languishing in jail
since 15.7.2022 having no criminal history, may
be enlarged on bail.

Learned A.G.A. also opposed the prayer for
bail.

From the averments made by learned counsel
for the parties madeat bar, prima facie there is no
material to suggest that based upon the applicant
given by  the informant, any further investigation
has been done. As of today, the post mortem
report on record indicates the cause of death as
ante mortem hanging and apart from ligature
mark, no other injury exists on the body of the
deceased irrespective of the future investigation, if
it happens.  As of today, there is no material to
suggest that the applicant had subjected the
deceased  to any physical or mental harassment in
relation to demand of dowry coupled with the fact
that the applicant being the husband languishing
in jail since 14.7.2024 having no criminal history
and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am
of the view that the applicant is entitled to be
released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant Abhishek Jaiswal be
released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.371 of
2024, under Sections 80/85 BNS & Section 3/4 of
the Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station Kotwali
Ayodhya, District Faizabad/ Ayodhya on his
furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties
of Rs.20,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court
concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to
undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence

similar to the offence of which he is accused or
suspected of the commission; and
(c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly
make any inducement, threat or promise to any
person acquainted with the facts of the case so as
to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the
Court or to any police officer or tamper with the
evidence.

title: BAIL No. 201600090922024 — Allahabad High Court, 27 Aug 2024 (Judge: KARUNESH SINGH PAWAR)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional
Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant
is not named in the first information report. The alleged
recovery of knife from the applicant is false. His name has
surfaced in the confessional statement of the co-accused
persons. The matter is triable by Magistrate. The applicant has
no previous criminal history. The applicant is in jail since
26.7.2024. 
It is further submitted that there is no possibility of the
applicant of fleeing away after being released on bail or
tampering with the witnesses. In case the applicant is enlarged
on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail but could not
dispute the aforesaid facts as argued by the learned counsel for
the applicant.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case,
including the fact that the applicant has no criminal history, the
offence is triable by Magistrate, arguments advanced by learned
counsel for the parties, for the period for which he is in jail and
without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I find
it to be a fit case for enlarging the applicant on bail.

Let the applicant Jalalu, involved in Case Crime No.230 of
2024 under Sections 3/8 of U.P. Prevention of Cow Slaughter
Act, P.S. Dubagga, district Lucknow be released on bail on his
furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like
amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the
following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of
justice:- 
(i) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the
trial. 
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution
witness. 
(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any
inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the
facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such
facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the
evidence. 
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he
shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence
when the witnesses are present in court. In case of default of
this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as
abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law. 
(v) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on
each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel. In case
of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may
proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal
Code. 
(vi) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial
and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section
82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the
court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial
court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with
law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

The bail application is allowed accordingly.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as
well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

In the light of the said allegation, learned
counsel for the applicant has drawn my attention
to  Annexure No.2 wherein an information was
given that the body of the deceased was lying  at

no weapon allegedly used has been recovered so
far and solely based upon the apprehension
expressed against the applicant, the applicant has
been linked with the offence in question.  Hence,
the applicant who is languishing in jail since
25.4.2024 having no criminal history, may be

enlarged on bail.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for
bail.

Considering the nature of the injuries
sustained by the deceased, there being no
independent witness to the incident and
considering the first report given by the informant
and the inquest report, a prima facie case for bail
is made out particularly when there is nothing on
record to demonstrate that the applicant who is
aged about 60 years, if enlarged on bail, would in
any manner, adversely affect the trial and without
expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view
that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

title: BAIL No. 201600083882024 — Allahabad High Court, 09 Aug 2024 (Judge: SAURABH LAVANIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A.
for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

The submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that the
applicant is an innocent person and he has falsely been implicated in
the case. It is further submitted on behalf of the applicant that two
cases have been shown in the gang chart against the applicant and in
all the cases, the applicant is on bail. It is also submitted that co
accused namely Anita and Ashu Kumar Saroj have already been
enlarged on bail by this Court vide order(s) dated 14.06.2024 passed
in Criminal Misc. Bail Application Nos. 6319 of 2024 and 6297 of
2024.

He also stated that considering the facts of the case, as stated above,
there are reasonable grounds for believing that the applicant is not
guilty of the offence under the Gangsters Act and that he would not
commit the offence while on bail. He also submitted that the applicant
while on bail would not commit any crime/offence nor would try to
tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses in any manner
whatsoever it may be.

Learned Counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is
languishing in jail in this matter since 14.07.2023 and there is no
apprehension that, if the facility of bail is granted to the applicant, he
may flee from the course of law or he will not appear before the Court
below, as also the evidence/material available on record is not strong
enough to raise a presumption that the applicant is guilty of the
offences mentioned in the gang chart.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for grant of bail, but has
fairly conceded that in the cases mentioned in the gang chart, the
applicant is on bail. He also could not dispute that co-accused persons
have already been enlarged on bail by this Court.

Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for parties,
material available on record as well as totality of fact and
circumstances as also the fact that co-accused persons have already
been enlarged on bail by this Court as also after taking note of Section
19(4)(b) of the Gangsters Act in light of the facts of the case and
submission of counsel for the applicant to the effect that while on bail
in this case, the applicant would not commit any crime/offence nor
would try to tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses in any
manner whatsoever it may be and without expressing any opinion on
the merits of the case, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to
be released on bail.

draws my attention to the medical done on the victim on the
same day i.e. 14.02.2023 at about 10:30 PM, wherein, the
victim was examined and no injury was observed in the internal
part of the victim. The hymen and perineum was found to be
intact. He further states that even in the opinion of the doctor,
there is no sign of use of force as appeared from the

examination. He thus argues that in terms of the mandate of
Section 375 IPC read with Section 3 of POCSO Act, for
invoking and punishing of an accused under Section 3 of
POCSO Act and under Section 375 of IPC, it is essential that
there should be a penetrative sexual assault as defined under
Section 3 of POCSO Act. He argues that in terms of the medical
on record, prima facie, there is no material whatsoever to even
alleged the commission of the offence under Section 3 of
POCSO Act or the commission of the act as defined under
Section 375 of IPC and the allegations, even if, treated to be
gospel truth, for the sake of argument would result in
prosecution under Section 7/8 of POCSO Act and not under
Section 5m as is being done by the prosecution, as such, the
applicant, who is in custody since 15.02.2023 and has criminal
history of two minor offences, may be enlarged on bail.

Learned A.G.A. as well as learned Counsel for the informant
vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima facie, as
per the allegations contained in the FIR and the two statements,
there is no specific allegation of wrong being done on 6 years
old victim, however, the medical on the same day does not
corroborate or even suggest the commission of the act as
defined under Section 375 of IPC or Section 3 of the POCSO
Act and also considering the medical report on record prima
facie the allegation against the applicant can be placed to an
offence under Section 7/8 of the POCSO Act and under Section
354 of IPC and the fact that the witnesses have already been
examined and the applicant is in custody since 15.02.2023, I am
of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

title: BAIL No. 201600079732024 — Allahabad High Court, 18 Sep 2024 (Judge: PANKAJ BHATIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and  learned 
A.G.A. for the State.

In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that on the basis of the
information received, a search team was constituted and on the
basis of the search carried out from the applicant allegedly 1 kg
275 gms charas was recovered.  In the light of the said
allegations, the submissions of the learned counsel is that there
is no material to suggest  the recovery was made from the
conscious possession at the instance of the applicant. He further
argues that there are no independent witness to the search. He
further argues that in the matter in which the sample was drawn
is contrary to the notification of the year, 2022 as well as
mandate of Section 52 A of the N.D.P.S. Act. He places reliance
upon judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in  Mohd
Muslim @ Hussain v. State (NCT of Delhi); 2023 LiveLaw
(SC) 260 and Yusuf @ Asif v. State; Criminal Appeal No.3191
of 2023 decided on 13.10.2023. He lastly argues that the
applicant has no criminal antecedents under N.D.P. Act and he
is in jail since 26.6.2024.

Learned A.G.A. opposes the bail application  and
submitted that In view of the bar created by Section 37 of the
N.D.P.S. Act, the bail application is liable to be rejected. He,
however, does not disputes the fact that the applicants have no
criminal antecedents under N.D.P.S Act.

Considering the arguments raised at bar, as the alleged
recovery is more than commercial quantity, the test of Section
37 has to be satisfied. The scope of Section 37 of NDPS Act
came up for consideration before the Supreme Court in Mohd

Muslim @ Hussain v. State (NCT of Delhi); 2023 LiveLaw
(SC) 260 wherein, interpreting Section 37, the Supreme Court
observed as under: 
"18. The conditions which courts have to be cognizant of are
that there are reasonable grounds for believing that the accused
is "not guilty of such offence" and that he is not likely to
commit any offence while on bail. What is meant by "not guilty"
when all the evidence is not before the court? It can only be a
prima facie determination. That places the court's discretion
within a very narrow margin. Given the mandate of the general
law on bails (Sections 436, 437 and 439, CrPC) which classify
offences based on their gravity, and instruct that certain serious
crimes have to be dealt with differently while considering bail
applications, the additional condition that the court should be
satisfied that the accused (who is in law presumed to be
innocent) is not guilty, has to be interpreted reasonably.
Further the classification of offences under Special Acts (NDPS
Act, etc.), which apply over and above the ordinary bail
conditions required to be assessed by courts, require that the
court records its satisfaction that the accused might not be
guilty of the offence and that upon release, they are not likely to
commit any offence. These two conditions have the effect of
overshadowing other conditions. In cases where bail is sought,
the court assesses the material on record such as the nature of
the offence, likelihood of the accused co-operating with the
investigation, not fleeing from justice: even in serious offences
like murder, kidnapping, rape, etc. On the other hand, the court
in these cases under such special Acts, have to address itself
principally on two facts: likely guilt of the accused and the
likelihood of them not committing any offence upon release.
This court has generally upheld such conditions on the ground
that liberty of such citizens have to - in cases when accused of
offences enacted under special laws – be balanced against the
public interest.

In the present case, prima facie, there was no independent
witness of the search, the mandate of Section 52-A has not be
followed. On these two discrepancies, prima facie view can be
formed that the prosecution may not be able to establish its case
against the applicant. It is clarified that this observation is only
for the purposes of consideration of bail and would not have
any adverse effect on trial. In respect of the second condition
specified under Section 37, as the applicant has no criminal
antecedents, in view of the law as laid down in the case of
Ranjitsing Brahmajeetsingh Sharma Vs. State of
Maharashtra & Anr: AIR 2005 Sc 2277, the second set of
Section 37 is also satisfied in the case of the applicant.

In view of the reason recorded as above, the applicant is
enlarged on bail. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

title: BAIL No. 201600078222024 — Allahabad High Court, 22 Aug 2024 (Judge: PANKAJ BHATIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well
as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer by
arguing that very huge quantity was recovered
from the applicant which cannot be planted by the
authorities and considering the huge recovery, the
bail application deserves to be rejected. He further
argues that as against the applicant, a case has
been registered under the Gangster Act after the
present FIR, thus his opposition is founded on
substantial and huge recovery effected from the

applicant.

Considering the submissions made at the Bar,
and the fact that the alleged recovery from the
applicant is more than the commercial quantity,
the test of Section 37 of the NDPS Act has to be
satisfied. Section 37 of the NDPS Act came up for
interpretation by the Supreme court in the case of 
Mohd Muslim @ Hussain vs. State (NCT of
Delhi) reported in 2023 Live Law (SC) 260,
wherein the Supreme Court interpreted Section 37
of the NDPS Act as under:- 
"18. The conditions which courts have to be cognizant of
are that there are reasonable grounds for believing that
the accused is "not guilty of such offence" and that he is
not likely to commit any offence while on bail. What is
meant by "not guilty" when all the evidence is not before
the court? It can only be prima facie determination. That
places the court's discretion within a very narrow margin.
Given the mandate of the general law on bails (Sections
436, 437 and 439, CrPC) which classify offences based on
their gravity, and instruct that certain serious crimes have
to be dealt with differently while considering bail
applications, the additional condition that the court should
be satisfied that the accused (who is in law presumed to
be innocent) is not guilty, has to be interpreted reasonably.
Further the classification of offences under Special Acts
(NDPS Act, etc.), which apply over and above the ordinary
bail conditions required to be assessed by courts, require
that the court records its satisfaction that the accused
might not be guilty of the offence and that upon release,
they are not likely to commit any offence. These two
conditions have the effect of overshadowing other
conditions. In cases where bail is sought, the court
assesses the material on record such as the nature of the
offence, likelihood of the accused co-operating with the
investigation, not fleeing from justice: even in serious
offences like murder, kidnapping, rape, etc. On the other
hand, the court in these cases under such special Acts,
have to address itself principally on two facts: likely guilt of
the accused and the likelihood of them not committing any
offence upon release. This court has generally upheld such
conditions on the ground that liberty of such citizens have
to - in cases when accused of offences enacted under
special laws ? be balanced against the public interest.

In the present case, the documents on record
including the counter affidavit are silent as to how
the recovery was effected from the recoveries
which were shown from the various accused, the
counter affidavit indicates that the FSL report
pertains to one sample of size 4.086 grams,
however, it is silent as to from which accused the
said sample was drawn and is also silent as to
whether sample was drawn from separate packets
allegedly recovered. In the statement before the
trial Court, P.W. 1 has specifically stated that he
was not aware of compliance of Section 52-A of
the NDPS Act, thus based upon these two
infirmities, which are apparent, prima facie, view
can be formed that the prosecution may not be
able to establish the charge against the applicant.
As the applicant has no criminal history,
considering the law as laid down in the case of
Ranjitsing Brahmajeetsing Sharma vs State
Of Maharashtra & Anr : AIR 2005 SC 2277,
the second test is also satisfied. Apart from the
infirmities referred above, there is no likelihood of
the trial being concluded in the near future and
relying on the judgment of the Supreme Court in
the case of  Jalaluddin Khan Versus Union of
India (Supra), the applicant is enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 112 of 2023, under

Nagar, District Barabanki,  on his furnishing

to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the

ARUN KUMAR 
High Court of Judicature at Allahabad, 
Lucknow Bench
Digitally signed by :-

A plain and literal interpretation of the conditions under
Section 37 (i.e., that Court should be satisfied that the
accused is not guilty and would not commit any offence)
would effectively exclude grant of bail altogether, resulting
in punitive detention and unsanctioned preventive

detention as well. Therefore, the only manner in which
such special conditions as enacted under Section 37 can
be considered within constitutional parameters is where
the court is reasonably satisfied on a prima facie look at
the material on record (whenever the bail application is
made) that the accused is not guilty. Any other
interpretation, would result in complete denial of the bail
to a person accused of offences such as those enacted
under Section 37 of the NDPS Act.

title: BAIL No. 201600070912024 — Allahabad High Court, 04 Jul 2024 (Judge: PANKAJ BHATIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned
A.G.A. and Sri Bal Krishna Shukla, who has filed Vakalatnama
on behalf of the complainant and perused the record.

The Counsel for the applicant further argues that the
allegations were levelled against all the matrimonial family
members. The applicant is in custody since 14.01.2024 and has
no criminal antecedents. The charge-sheet has been filed against
the applicant in the month of April, 2024. The investigation
with regard to the other co-accused is still going on and thus,
there is no likelihood of the trial being initiated or concluded in
near future, as such, the applicant may be enlarged on bail.

The Counsel for the informant, on the other hand, strongly
opposed the bail prayer by arguing that the victim was carrying
a male fetus also. He further argues that the information with
regard to the harassment was given two days earlier also, which
is evident from the FIR and subsequently, the matrimonial
family had killed after two days of the report of the first
incident of harassment and considering the fact that a female
victim has died along with a fetus, a clear case is made out
against the applicant and also considering the gravity of the
offence, the bail application should be rejected.

Learned A.G.A. also opposed the bail prayer by arguing that
from the perusal of the case diary and the supplementary
affidavit filed today, it appears that some suicide note was also
recovered, although, the gist of suicide note is a part of the case
diary, however, the extract is recorded in the case diary, which
records that on account of the conduct of the matrimonial
family, apparently, the victim had committed suicide.

Considering the aforesaid facts and material on record
including the submissions made at the bar, prima facie, what
transpires is that the death had occurred after three years of
marriage; from the postmortem report as well as the suicide
note, prima facie, it appears to be a suicide; in the suicide note
or even in the FIR, no specific allegations against the applicant
of causing mental and physical harassment to the victim in
relation to the demand of dowry soon before the death coupled
with the fact that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and
is languishing in jail since 14.01.2024 and there is nothing on
record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail,
would in any way adversely affect the trial, I am of the view
that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail. Accordingly,
the bail application is allowed.

title: BAIL No. 201600070612024 — Allahabad High Court, 03 Jul 2024 (Judge: SAURABH LAVANIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A.
for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

The submission of learned counsel for the applicant is that the
applicant is an innocent person and she has falsely been implicated in
the case. It is further submitted on behalf of the applicant that only one
case has been shown in the gang chart against the applicant and in that
case, the applicant is on bail.

He also stated that considering the facts of the case, as stated above,
there are reasonable grounds for believing that the applicant is not
guilty of the offence under the Gangsters Act and that he would not
commit the offence while on bail. He also submitted that the applicant
while on bail would not commit any crime/offence nor would try to
tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses in any manner
whatsoever it may be.

Learned Counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is
languishing in jail in this matter since 12.05.2024 and there is no
apprehension that, if the facility of bail is granted to the applicant, he
may flee from the course of law or she will not appear before the
Court below, as also the evidence/material available on record is not
strong enough to raise a presumption that the applicant is guilty of the
offences mentioned in the gang chart.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for grant of bail, but has
fairly conceded that in the cases mentioned in the gang chart, the
applicant is on bail.

Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for parties,
material available on record as well as totality of fact and

circumstances as also after taking note of Section 19(4)(b) of the
Gangsters Act in light of the facts of the case and submission of
counsel for the applicant to the effect that while on bail in this case,
the applicant would not commit any crime/offence nor would try to
tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses in any manner
whatsoever it may be and without expressing any opinion on the
merits of the case, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be
released on bail.

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well
as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the bail prayer by
arguing that as the recovery is more than the
commercial quantity, the bail application deserves
to be rejected in view of the bar under Section 37
of the NDPS Act.

Section 37 of the NDPS Act was interpreted by
the Supreme Court in the case of   Mohd Muslim
@ Hussain vs. State (NCT of Delhi) reported
in 2023 Live Law (SC) 260 to the following
effect:-
"18. The conditions which courts have to be
cognizant of are that there are reasonable
grounds for believing that the accused is "not
guilty of such offence" and that he is not likely to

commit any offence while on bail. What is meant
by "not guilty" when all the evidence is not before
the court? It can only be prima facie
determination. That places the court's discretion
within a very narrow margin. Given the mandate
of the general law on bails (Sections 436, 437 and
439, CrPC) which classify offences based on their
gravity, and instruct that certain serious crimes
have to be dealt with differently while considering
bail applications, the additional condition that the
court should be satisfied that the accused (who is
in law presumed to be innocent) is not guilty, has
to be interpreted reasonably. Further the
classification of offences under Special Acts (NDPS
Act, etc.), which apply over and above the
ordinary bail conditions required to be assessed by
courts, require that the court records its
satisfaction that the accused might not be guilty
of the offence and that upon release, they are not
likely to commit any offence. These two conditions
have the effect of overshadowing other conditions.
In cases where bail is sought, the court assesses
the material on record such as the nature of the
offence, likelihood of the accused co-operating
with the investigation, not fleeing from justice:
even in serious offences like murder, kidnapping,
rape, etc. On the other hand, the court in these
cases under such special Acts, have to address
itself principally on two facts: likely guilt of the
accused and the likelihood of them not committing
any offence upon release. This court has generally
upheld such conditions on the ground that liberty
of such citizens have to - in cases when accused of
offences enacted under special laws ? be balanced
against the public interest.

In the present case, prima facie, the mandate of
Section 52-A of the NDPS Act has not been
followed. There are no independent witnesses to
the search, as such, a prima facie can be formed
that the prosecution may not be able to establish
the offence based upon these discrepancies. As
the applicants have no criminal history of an
offence under the NDPS Act, the second test of
Section 37 of the NDPS Act is also satisfied in
favour of the applicants.

For the reasoning recorded above, the
applicants who are in custody since 25.03.2024
are enlarged on bail.  Accordingly, the bail
application is allowed.

Ramsunder Gond,

information was received from her aunt that in between the
father and the applicant, who was the brother of the informant,
a fight took place. When the informant reached home, it was

altercation has taken place in between the applicant and his

contusion injuries. The cause of death, as per the postmortem

Counsel for the applicant is that the applicant is the son of the
deceased and the evidence on record prima facie suggests that
on account of altercation, the death had occurred however, there
is no evidence to suggest that there was any mens rea or
knowledge that the said act would result into the death. The
deponent in the present case is the mother of the informant.
Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima facie, as
per the material on record, the death had occurred on account of

an altercation and subsequent fight in between the father and
the son; the applicant, who is son of the deceased, is also
present at the time of postmortem, prima facie the ingredients to
attract Section 304 may not be applicable to the facts of the

coupled with the fact that the applicant has no criminal

the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

Heard Sri Atul Verma, Amarjeet Rakhra and Sri Sudhanshu

learned A.G.A. and Sri Vaibhav Upadhyay, who has filed
Vakalatnama on behalf of the complainant and perused the
record. The Vakalatnama is taken on record.

It is further argued by the Counsel for the applicant that the
entire case is premised on forming physical relation on the false
pretext of marriage apart from the allegations which necessarily
indicate that the physical relations continued in between them
over a span of almost one and a half years. He further argues
that prima facie, it is case of consensual relation in between two
adults and thus, the applicant, who is in custody since
10.05.2024, should be enlarged on bail. The criminal history of
the applicant has been duly explained, which are not of similar
nature.

The Counsel for the complainant strongly opposes the bail
prayer by arguing that the applicant is aide of some gangster
and there is all likelihood that the victim would be harassed and
therefore considering the gravity of the offence, the bail
application should be rejected. He further argues that the
tentative age of the applicant is around 45 years. The applicant
is already a married man. He further argues that the allegation
that the victim is a married woman, is wrong and there is no
material and even from the FIR, nothing can be deciphered that
the victim was married woman. He further argues that during
the course of collecting evidence, the presence of the applicant
was found at Hotel Taj.

Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer by
praying that the charge-sheet has already been filed on
22.05.2024. He also opposes the bail application by arguing that
the offence alleged against the applicant is grievous in nature
and therefore, the bail application should be rejected.

Considering the allegations made at the bar, prima facie, in
terms of the allegations physical relations continued in between
the applicant and the victim over a span of almost one and a
half years; the complainant is well known with the criminal
justice system as earlier she herself had lodged an FIR against
the applicant under Section 498A IPC read with Section 3/4 of
D.P. Act; prima facie, there is no explanation as to why the FIR
has been lodged after a substantial long period of time; the age
of the victim is 32 years which reflects that the complainant is
of reasonable maturity; the charge-sheet has been filed coupled
with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 10.05.2024
and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant
if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial, I
am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on
bail. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

title: BAIL No. 201600062902024 — Allahabad High Court, 13 Jun 2024 (Judge: SAURABH LAVANIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A.
for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

The submissions of learned counsel for the applicants is that the
applicants are innocent persons and they have falsely been implicated
in the case. It is further submitted on behalf of the applicants that four
cases have been shown in the gang chart against the applicant no. 1
and in all the cases, the applicant no. 1 is on bail. It is also submitted
that three cases have been shown in the gang chart against the
applicant no. 2 and in all the cases, the applicant no. 2 is on bail.

He also stated that considering the facts of the case, as stated above,
there are reasonable grounds for believing that the applicants are not
guilty of the offence under the Gangsters Act and that they would not
commit the offence while on bail. He also submitted that the
applicants while on bail would not commit any crime/offence nor
would try to tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses in any
manner whatsoever it may be.

Learned Counsel for the applicants has submitted that applicants are
languishing in jail in this matter since 03.05.2024 and there is no
apprehension that, if the facility of bail is granted to the applicants,
they may flee from the course of law or they will not appear before the
Court below, as also the evidence/material available on record is not
strong enough to raise a presumption that the applicants are guilty of
the offences mentioned in the gang chart.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for grant of bail, but has
fairly conceded that in the cases mentioned in the gang chart, the

applicants are on bail.

Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for parties,
material available on record as well as totality of fact and
circumstances as also after taking note of Section 19(4)(b) of the
Gangsters Act in light of the facts of the case and submission of
counsel for the applicants to the effect that while on bail in this case,
the applicants would not commit any crime/offence nor would try to
tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses in any manner
whatsoever it may be and without expressing any opinion on the
merits of the case, I am of the view that the applicants are entitled to
be released on bail.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned

complete instructions in the matter as such this Court proceeded

application, submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in this

complicity of the applicant has surfaced in the confessional statements of
co-accused persons, namely, Rajnish Saket, however, he and co-accused
Mohd. Jameel have already been granted bail by this Court vide orders
13.3.2024 and 18.04.2024 passed in Crl. Misc. Bail Application Nos. 2838
of 2024 and 3994 of 2024.

Vide order dated 27.05.2024, this Court allowed the Criminal
Misc. Bail Application No. 5751 of 2024 filed by co-accused
Mohd. Kaif and enlarged the co-accused on bail. The relevant
portion of the order dated 27.05.2024 reads as under: 
"1. Heard learned counsel for the accused-applicant as well as learned
A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.  Learned A.G.A. informs that
he has procured complete instructions in the matter, including upto date
case diary and, charge-sheet in this case has already been filed.

applicant on the ground that the offence has been committed in a brutal

any opinion on the merits of the case, I am of the view that

title: BAIL No. 201600057342024 — Allahabad High Court, 25 May 2024 (Judge: SAURABH LAVANIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicants as well as learned A.G.A.
for the State of U.P. and perused the record.

The submissions of learned counsel for the applicants is that the
applicants are innocent persons and they have falsely been implicated
in the case. It is further submitted on behalf of the applicants that one
case has been shown against in the gang chart against the applicant no.
1 and three cases have been shown against in the gang chart against
the applicant no. 2.

He also stated that considering the facts of the case, as stated above,
there are reasonable grounds for believing that the applicants are not
guilty of the offence under the Gangsters Act and that he would not
commit the offence while on bail. He also submitted that the
applicants while on bail would not commit any crime/offence nor
would try to tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses in any
manner whatsoever it may be.

Learned Counsel for the applicants has submitted that applicants are
languishing in jail in this matter since 05.10.2020 and there is no
apprehension that, if the facility of bail is granted to the applicants, he
may flee from the course of law or he will not appear before the Court
below, as also the evidence/material available on record is not strong
enough to raise a presumption that the applicants are guilty of the
offences mentioned in the gang chart.

Learned A.G.A. has opposed the prayer for grant of bail, but has
fairly conceded that in the cases mentioned in the gang chart, the
applicants are on bail.

Considering the rival submissions of learned counsel for parties,
material available on record as well as totality of fact and
circumstances as also after taking note of Section 19(4)(b) of the
Gangsters Act in light of the facts of the case and submission of
counsel for the applicants to the effect that while on bail in this case,
the applicants would not commit any crime/offence nor would try to
tamper the evidence or influence the witnesses in any manner
whatsoever it may be and without expressing any opinion on the
merits of the case, I am of the view that the applicants are entitled to
be released on bail.

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned
A.G.A. and perused the record.

In terms of the FIR lodged on 16.03.2024, it was alleged that
on 03.06.2023 at about 9:30 AM, the complainant was going for
some work when the co-accused Vikas along with two unknown
persons came on motorcycle and took the victim on an
unknown place where rape was committed on her and
inappropriate video was also made. In the statement under
Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C., the victim reiterated the said
statement. The name of the applicant was not taken in the
statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C. or in the FIR or in the
statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C. There is no recovery of
any inappropriate videos and the independent witnesses have
also stated that they have never seen any inappropriate videos.
The I.O. on the basis of CDR report saw that the co-accused
Vikas used to talk to the victim even after the alleged date of
incident which prima facie demonstrates that both were
friendly.
Learned A.G.A. vehemently opposed the bail prayer.

Considering the inordinate delay in lodging the FIR, the
name of the applicant not surfacing either in the FIR or in the
statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.; the analysis report of
the CDR; no appropriate video has been recovered and the fact
that the applicant has no criminal antecedents and is
languishing in jail since 27.03.2024, I am of the view that the
applicant is entitled to be released on bail. Accordingly, the bail
application is allowed.

of the prosecutirx under Sections 147, 452, 323, 504, 506, 427,
392 I.P.C. and Section 3(1)(Da), 3(1)(Dha) of SC/ST Act. It has
been stated that it is only as a counter-blast that the first

information report has been lodged against the applicant.

It is submitted by learned counsel for applicant that applicant
is languishing in jail since 23.04.2024. The counsel contends
that there is no possibility of the applicant fleeing away from
justice or tampering with the witnesses. In case the applicant is
enlarged on bail, he shall not misuse the liberty of bail.

It is further submitted by learned counsel for the applicant
that he also seeks parity inasmuch as other co-accused persons
of the case have been enlarged on bail thereby co-accused Jais
Ram has been enlarged on bail by this Court by means of order
dated 25.08.2021, passed in Bail No. 10358 of 2019 and one
more co-accused namely Rajit Ram has also been enlarged on
bail by order of same date passed in Bail No. 11395 of 2019. It
is submitted that allegedly role of petitioner being the same as
that other co-accused persons who have been enlarged on bail,
the applicant may also be enlarged on bail.

Learned A.G.A. on the other hand though opposed the bail
applicant but could not dispute the aforesaid facts and has fairly
conceded that co-accused persons namely Jais Ram and Rajit
Ram have been already enlarged on bail.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, perusing
the record and also considering the fact that there is no
explanation for the delay in either reporting the matter to the
police or even filing of the complaint under Section 156(3) of
the Cr.P.C. It has also unexplained that as to why the
prosecutrix herself is the complainant refused to undergo
medical examination and also considering the fact that just
nearly two months earlier a first information report was lodged
by the father of the applicant against the Jeth of the prosecutrix
and probably the said proceedings have been initiated by the
prosecutrix in the mala fide manner and also considering the
fact that two co-accused of the case namely Jais Ram and Rajit
Ram have already been enlarged on bail, I consider it is a fit
case of grant of bail. the nature of allegations, arguments
advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and, without
expressing any opinion on the merit of the case, I find it to be a
fit case for granting bail.

title: BAIL No. 201600052992024 — Allahabad High Court, 02 Jul 2024 (Judge: PANKAJ BHATIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant,
Mohd. Tabrez Iqbal, learned counsel for the
complainant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused
the record.

Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn
my attention to the whattsapp chats in between
the applicant and the victim which demonstrates
the closeness and the proximity of the victim with
the applicant.  The tentative age of the victim is
around 25 years.

Learned counsel for the applicant has placed
reliance on the judgement of the  Hon'ble Supreme
Court in the case of Deepak Gulati Vs. State of
Haryana : AIR 2013 SC 2071 to argue that
admittedly physical relations continued  
in
between the parties over a span of almost two
years, as such no case can be said to be made out
against the applicant.   The applicant is in custody
since 16.4.2024 and has no criminal antecedents,
hence the applicant may be released on bail.

Learned counsel for the informant as well as
learned A.G.A. strongly opposed the prayer for bail
by arguing that the victim was friendly to the
applicant, however after administering something
in the cold drinks, she became unconscious and
the applicant committed wrong on her and
thereafter under the threat of making
inappropriate videos viral, on various occasions,
physical relations were formed under the threat.  
Similar statements were given under Section 164
Cr.P.C.  Hence, the bail application may be
rejected.

Considering the law laid down by Hon'ble
Supreme Court in the case of Deepak Gulati Vs.
State of Haryana : AIR 2013 SC 2071, coupled 
with the fact that the entire case is premised on
forming physical relations on false pretext of
marriage which continued for a span of two years,
and the fact that the applicant has no criminal
antecedents and is languishing in jail since
16.4.2024 and there is nothing on record to
demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail,
would in any way adversely affect the trial and
without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of
the view that the applicant is entitled to be
released on bail.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned
A.G.A. and perused the record.

Learned counsel for the applicant has drawn my attention to
the post mortem report which indicates the cause of death as
Asphyxia due to ante mortem hanging and apart from ligature
mark, two abraded contusions were seen on the head and and
the side of the knee of the deceased which according to the
applicant, can be resulted while lowering the body of the
deceased. The applicant is the husband of the deceased. It is
further argued that there is nothing against the applicant to
demonstrate that soon before the death, the deceased was
subjected to any physical or mental torture in relation to
demand of dowry at the instance of the applicant. The applicant
is in jail since 9.11.2023 having no criminal history, hence he

title: BAIL No. 201600051432024 — Allahabad High Court, 29 May 2024 (Judge: PANKAJ BHATIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and
Shri Ran Vijay Singh, learned A.G.A. for the  and
perused the record.

The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case
Crime No.289 of 2023 under sections 8/21/29 of
N.D.P.S. Act, Police Station Lonikatra, District
Barabanki.

It is further argued on behalf of the applicant
that the all the co accused were enlarged on bail,
although on different grounds and the applicant
does not claim parity with the said co accused.  
Hence, the  applicant may be enlarged on bail.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail by
arguing that a huge quantity of morphine weighing
about 8.166 kgs. was recovered from the vehicle
driven by the applicant as such the bail application
has to be rejected in view of the restrictions
imposed by virtue of Section 37 of the N.D.P.S.Act. 
He further drawn my attention to the fact that the
F.S.L. report on record contained in page 18 of the
counter affidavit tested the samples as heroine, as
such, the  bail application should be rejected.

Learned counsel for the applicant in the
rejoinder affidavit argued that the samples size as

per the F.S.L. report relied upon by the learned
A.G.A.  weighs 4.937 gms. and there is no
indication as to from which of the twenty three
packets seized simultaneously, the said sample
was drawn as such the manner of sampling, timing
of sampling and not following the mandate of
Section 52-A are apparent infirmities by the
prosecution.

Hon'ble Supreme Court had the occasion to
deal with the aspect of Section 37 and the
conditions prescribed therein in the case of Mohd
Muslim @ Hussain vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 260.  While
dealing with the scope of Section 37, Hon'ble Apex
Court observed as under:- 
"18. The conditions which courts have to be cognizant of
are that there are reasonable grounds for believing that
the accused is "not guilty of such offence" and that he is
not likely to commit any offence while on bail. What is
meant by "not guilty" when all the evidence is not before
the court? It can only be prima facie determination. That
places the court's discretion within a very narrow margin.
Given the mandate of the general law on bails (Sections
436, 437 and 439, CrPC) which classify offences based on
their gravity, and instruct that certain serious crimes have
to be dealt with differently while considering bail
applications, the additional condition that the court should
be satisfied that the accused (who is in law presumed to

be innocent) is not guilty, has to be interpreted reasonably.
Further the classification of offences under Special Acts
(NDPS Act, etc.), which apply over and above the ordinary
bail conditions required to be assessed by courts, require
that the court records its satisfaction that the accused
might not be guilty of the offence and that upon release,
they are not likely to commit any offence. These two
conditions have the effect of overshadowing other
conditions. In cases where bail is sought, the court
assesses the material on record such as the nature of the
offence, likelihood of the accused co-operating with the
investigation, not fleeing from justice: even in serious
offences like murder, kidnapping, rape, etc. On the other
hand, the court in these cases under such special Acts,
have to address itself principally on two facts: likely guilt of
the accused and the likelihood of them not committing any
offence upon release. This court has generally upheld such
conditions on the ground that liberty of such citizens have
to - in cases when accused of offences enacted under
special laws – be balanced against the public interest.

title: BAIL No. 201600047252024 — Allahabad High Court, 02 Jul 2024 (Judge: PANKAJ BHATIA)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and
learned A.G.A. for the  and perused the record.

The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case
Crime No.43 of 2024 under sections 8/21 of
N.D.P.S. Act, Police Station Behtgokul, District
Hardoi.

Learned counsel for the applicant has argued
that the recovery of the alleged substance was not
effected in accordance with law.  There were no
independent witnesses to the search.  It is further
argued that the mandate of Section 52-A as well
as two standing orders were not followed.   He
lastly argued that the applicant  is in custody since
17.2.2024 having no criminal history of an offence
under the N.D.P.S. Act or any other offence, hence,
the  applicant may be enlarged on bail.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail by
arguing that the recovery is more than the

commercial quantity, which is 100 grams in the
case of Alprazolam, as such the bail application
has to be rejected.

Hon'ble Supreme Court had the occasion to
deal with the aspect of Section 37 and the
conditions prescribed therein in the case of Mohd
Muslim @ Hussain vs. State (NCT of Delhi)
reported in 2023 Live Law (SC) 260.  While
dealing with the scope of Section 37, Hon'ble Apex
Court observed as under:- 
"18. The conditions which courts have to be cognizant of
are that there are reasonable grounds for believing that
the accused is "not guilty of such offence" and that he is
not likely to commit any offence while on bail. What is
meant by "not guilty" when all the evidence is not before
the court? It can only be prima facie determination. That
places the court's discretion within a very narrow margin.
Given the mandate of the general law on bails (Sections
436, 437 and 439, CrPC) which classify offences based on
their gravity, and instruct that certain serious crimes have
to be dealt with differently while considering bail
applications, the additional condition that the court should
be satisfied that the accused (who is in law presumed to
be innocent) is not guilty, has to be interpreted reasonably.
Further the classification of offences under Special Acts
(NDPS Act, etc.), which apply over and above the ordinary
bail conditions required to be assessed by courts, require
that the court records its satisfaction that the accused
might not be guilty of the offence and that upon release,

they are not likely to commit any offence. These two
conditions have the effect of overshadowing other
conditions. In cases where bail is sought, the court
assesses the material on record such as the nature of the
offence, likelihood of the accused co-operating with the
investigation, not fleeing from justice: even in serious
offences like murder, kidnapping, rape, etc. On the other
hand, the court in these cases under such special Acts,
have to address itself principally on two facts: likely guilt of
the accused and the likelihood of them not committing any
offence upon release. This court has generally upheld such
conditions on the ground that liberty of such citizens have
to - in cases when accused of offences enacted under
special laws – be balanced against the public interest.
Thus, the bail application is allowed.

title: BAIL No. 201600044522024 — Allahabad High Court, 16 May 2024 (Judge: MOHD. FAIZ ALAM KHAN)

paragraphs.text:
Heard Ms. Jyoti Rawat, learned counsel for the accused-
applicant as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused
the record.

It is further submitted that the F.I.R. of this case has been
lodged by the informant on 24.06.2022 at 06.13 p.m. at Police
Station Haiderganj, District Ayodhya alleging therein that on
23-06-2022 at about 01:00p.m. Manoj Modanwal and Ravikant
Modanwal had left their home on a motor cycle, but they did
not return till evening and on 24-06-2022, it was informed
through social media that they have been done to death by some
unknown persons.

Learned A.G.A. opposes the prayer of bail of the applicant on
the ground that the applicant along with other accused persons
has committed a heinous offence and this case pertains to
double murder, where two innocent persons have been done to
death with brutality and having regard to the material/evidence
available against the applicant, he is not entitled to be released
on bail.

It is further submitted that the  manner in which two
innocent persons have been  done to death is itself sufficient
enough to reject the bail application of the applicant, however,
he could not concern that the facility of bail applications have
been extended by the Coordinate Benches of this Court to those
who have taken active part in the 'marpeet' while no such
allegations have been revealed against the applicant.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having
perused the record, it is evident that dead bodies of two persons
were found at Kasba Haiderganj, Ayodhya bypass near
Saraswati Gyan Mandir and they were later on identified as
Ravikant Modanwal and Manoj Modanwal. The F.I.R. was
lodged by Dilip Kumar Modanwal in this regard stating that on
23.06.2022 at about 01:00pm, both the deceased persons had
gone on a motorcycle, but did not return till evening and also
did not attend their phone call and on 24.06.2022, they came to
know that they have been done to death by some unknown
persons and their dead bodies were found near Saraswati Gyan
Mandir. C.D.R. of the mobile phones of the deceased persons
was collected on the basis of which it was found that calls were

made on a particular phone number, which was found of one
Meera Modanwal, wife of the instant applicant, who on
interrogation confessed to the tune that one of the deceased
namely Ravikant Modanwal was talking to her daughter Priya
@ Jyoti Modanwal and have also made an obscene video of her
and also clicked some photographs, which he was posting at
social platform and when this was known to them, her son
Sandeep had scolded her and has also deleted the mobile
number of Ravikant Modanwal from the mobile phone of Priya
@ Jyoti Modanwal, however, Ravikant Modanwal continued to
remain in touch with Priya @ Jyoti Modanwal. On 22.06.2022
Ravikant Modanwal had made a call on her phone number and
proposed to marry Priya @ Jyoti Modanwal on which they
agreed to meet with the condition that Ravikant Modanwal
would bring her mother, however, on 23.06.2022, when Meera
Modanwal had gone to the lane situated at railway crossing of
Goshainganj, Ravikant Modanwal came there alone on which
she asked as to why he had not brought his mother, he informed
that she had come with his friend Manoj Modanwal. In the
meantime her son Sandeep had come home to take lunch and
got information of their meeting and he called Ramesh Kumar
Verma and they met with Ravikant Modanwal and his friend
Manoj Modanwal and they took both Ravikant Modanwal and
his friend Manoj Modanwal behind Indrabali School and
assaulted them. Sandeep also called his friend Sheru, thereafter
Ramesh Kumar Verma and Sheru had taken Ravikant
Modanwal behind Indrabali School, in the meantime, Sandeep
had also called his maternal uncle Ram Babu and Rohit and
they assaulted Ravikant Modanwal and from there they went to
the shop of Ramesh, where the condition of Ravikant
Modanwal deteriorated and when it was felt that he had died,
they were taken to the marriage hall of Ved Prakash Pathak,
where three labours namely Dilip, Chhotu and Manish were
present and when they inferred that Ravikant Modanwal had
died, they had assaulted Manoj Modanwal also in order to
screen the offence.

The statement of Priya @ Jyoti Modanwal, with whom one
of the deceased Ravikant Modanwal was having affair, was also
recorded by the investigating officer, who has corroborated the

title: BAIL No. 201600042572024 — Allahabad High Court, 04 Jul 2024 (Judge: PANKAJ BHATIA)

paragraphs.text:
The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case
Crime No.402 of 2023 under section 8/21/29 of
N.D.P.S. Act, P.S. - Zaidpur, District Barabanki.

In terms of the F.I.R., it was alleged that on the
basis of the information received, a search carried
out and on a motorcycle, the applicant was
apprehended and he was found carrying a bag
containing 915 grams of a powder.  On admission
of the applicant, that the said powder was heroin,
the applicant was arrested on the spot and arrest
memo was also prepared.  The F.I.R. is said to have
been lodged on 19.9.2023 at 5.44.

Learned counsel for the applicant has argued
that the aforesaid illegality itself renders the entire
recovery suspected.   He further argued that the
manner in which he sample was drawn, is neither
stated in the F.I.R. nor in the counter affidavit.  He
further argued that there was no independent
witness  to the search and further the mandate of
Section 52-A of the N.D.P.S. Act was not followed.  
As regards the criminal antecedents of the
applicant, it is argued that the applicant has one
criminal history in which the applicant has been
enlarged on bail, as has been disclosed in
paragraph 35 of the affidavit filed in support of the
second bail application.

Learned A.G.A. has strongly opposed the prayer
for bail by arguing that the recovery is more than
the commercial quantity which is 250 grams in the
case of heroin.  He further argued that the F.S.L.
report has corroborated that the recovered goods
are heroine. The F.S.L. report is filed alongwith
counter affidavit.  It is further argued that as per
Section 37 of the N.D.P.S. Act, bail of the applicant
should be rejected.

Considering the submissions made at the bar,
prima facie it appears that the arrest memo was
prepared at about 3.30 a.m., however it bears
F.I.R. number which was registered at 5.44 a.m. on

the same day.   Apart from the said, the manner of
drawing sample has not been indicated.  F.S.L.
report also records the sample size to be 4.496
grams which is less than he sample size prescribed
by virtue of Notification dated 23.12.2022. 
Furthermore, the mandate of Section 37 and
Section 52-A of the N.D.P.S. Act have not been
followed.

The true intent and interpretation of Section
37 of the Act was considered by Hon'ble Supreme
Court in the case of Mohd Muslim @ Hussain
vs. State (NCT of Delhi) reported in 2023
Live Law (SC) 260, to the following effect
(paragraphs 18, 19 and 20) :- 
"18. The conditions which courts have to be cognizant of
are that there are reasonable grounds for believing that
the accused is "not guilty of such offence" and that he is
not likely to commit any offence while on bail. What is
meant by "not guilty" when all the evidence is not before
the court? It can only be prima facie determination. That
places the court's discretion within a very narrow margin.
Given the mandate of the general law on bails (Sections
436, 437 and 439, CrPC) which classify offences based on
their gravity, and instruct that certain serious crimes have
to be dealt with differently while considering bail
applications, the additional condition that the court should
be satisfied that the accused (who is in law presumed to
be innocent) is not guilty, has to be interpreted reasonably.
Further the classification of offences under Special Acts
(NDPS Act, etc.), which apply over and above the ordinary
bail conditions required to be assessed by courts, require
that the court records its satisfaction that the accused
might not be guilty of the offence and that upon release,
they are not likely to commit any offence. These two
conditions have the effect of overshadowing other
conditions. In cases where bail is sought, the court

assesses the material on record such as the nature of the
offence, likelihood of the accused co-operating with the
investigation, not fleeing from justice: even in serious
offences like murder, kidnapping, rape, etc. On the other
hand, the court in these cases under such special Acts,
have to address itself principally on two facts: likely guilt of
the accused and the likelihood of them not committing any
offence upon release. This court has generally upheld such
conditions on the ground that liberty of such citizens have
to - in cases when accused of offences enacted under
special laws – be balanced against the public interest.

Additional Government Advocate for the State and

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the
gang chart three cases has been shown against the
applicant. In all the three cases, the applicant has been
enlarged on bail. The bail orders are annexed with the
affidavit filed in support of the bail application as
Annexures-3,4 and 5. Apart from the three cases, there is
one more case pending against the applicant. The bail
order is also on record as Annexure-6 to the bail
application. Except the above cases, there is no other
criminal history of the applicant. The applicant is in jail
since 31.1.2024.

namely Raj Kashyap and Sonu Kashyap alias Chhanga
have already been enlarged on bail by this Court.  Their
bail orders are on record as Annexures 7 and 8 to the bail
application.  Learned Counsel for the applicant claims
parity with the bail orders of co-accused persons.

an undertaking in terms of requirement of Section 19(4)(b)

Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned

taken on record.

The Counsel for the informant strongly opposes the bail
application by firstly arguing that in the affidavit, the
relationship of the deponent with the applicant has not been
disclosed. He places reliance on the order dated 10.04.20219
passed in Bail No.3690 of 2019 (Dharmendra Singh vs State of
U.P.), wherein, the Court had directed the Senior Registrar to
ensure that without disclosing the relation between the deponent

rejected.

the FIR and in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., there

was not named in the statement under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
and subsequently, in the statement under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.,

title: BAIL No. 201600040512024 — Allahabad High Court, 16 Apr 2024 (Judge: KARUNESH SINGH PAWAR)

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned Additional
Government Advocate for the State and perused the record.

Learned counsel for the applicant submits that in the gang
chart, one case has been shown against the applicant. In the
solitary case, the applicant has been enlarged on bail. The bail
order is annexed with the affidavit filed in support of the bail
application as Annexure-3. Apart from that case, there is no
other case pending against the applicant. The applicant is in jail
since 11.12.2023.

Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail prayer and
submits that the investigation is pending.

On due consideration to the arguments advanced by counsel
for the parties, perusal of the record as also the fact that in the
single case shown in the gang charte the applicant has been
enlarged on bail and he no other criminal history, the applicant
is in jail since 1.12.2023 and without expressing any opinion on

the merits of the case, I find it to be a fit case for enlarging the
applicant on bail.

Let the applicant Anil Verma, involved in Case Crime No.320
of 2023, under Sections 3(1) U.P. Gangsters & Anti Social
Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986, P.S.Tarun, district
Ayodhya/Faizabad be released on bail on his furnishing a
personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the
satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions
which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(1) The applicant will not tamper with the evidence during the
trial.
(ii) The applicant will not pressurize/ intimidate the prosecution
witness.
(iii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any
inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with
the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such
facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the
evidence.
(iv) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he
shall not seek any adjournment on the dates fixed for evidence
when the witnesses are present in court. In case of default of
this condition, it shall be open for the trial court to treat it as
abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(v) The applicant shall also file an undertaking in terms of 
requirement of Section 19(4)(b) of U.P. Gangsters & Anti Social 
Activities (Prevention) Act, 1986 that he will not indulge in any 
case or misuse the liberty of bail. 
(vi) The applicant shall remain present before the trial court on
each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel. In
case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the trial court may
proceed against him under Section 229-A of the Indian Penal

Code.
(vii) In case the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial
and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section
82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the
court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial
court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with
under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.

The bail application is allowed accordingly.

paragraphs.text:
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Sri  Vinay Kumar
Singh, learned counsel for the informant and learned AGA and
perused the record.

The accused-applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.440 of
2023 under Sections 304B, 498A IPC, 3/4 Dowry Prohibition
Act, Police Station Imaliya Sultanpur, District Sitapur.

In the light of the aforesaid allegations, it is argued by
learned counsel for the applicant who is mother-in-law of the
deceased that as per the post mortem report, cause of death is
ante mortem hanging and apart from ligature mark, no other
injury was visible on the body of the deceased.

Counsel for the informant on the other hand, strongly
opposes the bail application by arguing that on 16.11.2023, the
victim was beaten up by the matrimonial family and the
informant had paid Rs.10,000/- in cash and thus, no case for
bail is made out and the bail application may be rejected.

Considering the submissions made at the bar, prima facie in
terms of the FIR general allegations of demand of dowry have
been leveled as many as 9 persons of the matrimonial family,
post mortem on record does not indicate any visible injury on
the body of the deceased except ligature mark, the applicant is
mother-in-law and there is no specific allegation against the
applicant that soon before the death, the applicant had harassed
the victim either mentally or physically in relation to demand of
dowry, the applicant who is in custody since 11.12.2023 having
no criminal history, is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
Thus the bail application is allowed.

title: BAIL No. 201600036232024 — Allahabad High Court, 29 Jul 2024 (Judge: RAJESH SINGH CHAUHAN)

paragraphs.text:
Heard Sri Syed Ahmad Mehdi, learned counsel for the
applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

While rejecting the second bail application vide order dated
05.05.2023, this Court has passed the following order:-
"Heard learned counsel appearing for the accused-applicant and Sri
Ashwini Kumar Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State. 
This is second bail application which has been filed seeking bail in FIR
No.18 of 2020 under Sections 498A, 304B IPC, 3/4 Dowry Prohibition
Act, Police Station Summanpur, District Ambedkar Nagar. 
First bail application has been rejected by this Court vide order dated
25.05.2022 passed in Bail No.7824 of 2020 by following order:- 
"1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, Mr.Ashwini Kumar Singh,
learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

As per the learned counsel for the applicant, the present
applicant is in jail since 06.02.2020 in FIR/Case Crime No. 18
of 2020, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 of the
Dowry Prohibition Act, Police Station- Summanpur, District-
Ambedkar Nagar.

Let a copy of this order is forwarded to the trial Court concerned." 
I do not find any change circumstance to enlarge the accused-applicant on
bail at this stage. This bail application is rejected. However, learned trial
court is directed to expedite the trial and conclude the same preferably
within a period of six months."

Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that the
present applicant has been falsely implicated in the case as he
has not committed any offence as alleged. As a matter of fact
applicant's relation with his wife was cordial and they were
happily living as husband and wife. He has further submitted
that six fact/relevant witnesses have been examined and copies
thereof have been enclosed with the affidavit filed in support of

the application showing that out of six prosecution witnesses,
five prosecution witnesses have turned hostile.

Hence, keeping in view the pace of the trial, the trial would
not be concluded shortly, therefore considering the fact that the
present applicant is in jail since 06.02.2020 i.e about four years
and six months, out of total fifteen prosecution witnesses, six
prosecution witnesses have been examined, who are mainly
fact/relevant witnesses and out of them five prosecution
witnesses have turned hostile. Therefore, total period of
incarceration of the present applicant and also his fundamental
right of this speedy trial under Article 21 of the Constitution of
India, which is being flouted, the present applicant maybe
enlarged on bail.

title: BAIL No. 201600036042024 — Allahabad High Court, 05 Jun 2024 (Judge: SUBHASH VIDYARTHI)

paragraphs.text:
Heard Sri Sumeet Tahilramani, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri
Ranvijay Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the records.

In the affidavit filed in support of bail application it has been stated
that the applicant is innocent, he has been falsely implicated in the
present case and he has no criminal history.

The learned A.G.A. I has drawn attention of the Court to the
provisions contained in Section 37 of the NDPS Act, which is as
follows: -

The learned A.G.A.-I has relied upon the judgments in the cases of
State by the Inspector of Police versus B. Ramu, 2024 INSC 114,
S.L.P. Crl. No. 8137 of 2022, decided on 12.02.2024, Union of India
v. Ajay Kumar Singh, 2023 SCC OnLine SC 346 and Mohd.
Muslim v. State (NCT of Delhi), 2023 SCC OnLine SC 352.

In Mohd. Muslim (Supra), the Hon’ble Supreme Court held that: -
“20. A plain and literal interpretation of the conditions under
Section 37 (i.e., that Court should be satisfied that the accused is
not guilty and would not commit any offence) would effectively
exclude grant of bail altogether, resulting in punitive detention
and unsanctioned preventive detention as well. Therefore, the
only manner in which such special conditions as enacted under
Section 37 can be considered within constitutional parameters is
where the court is reasonably satisfied on a prima facie look at
the material on record (whenever the bail application is made)
that the accused is not guilty. Any other interpretation, would
result in complete denial of the bail to a person accused of
offences such as those enacted under Section 37 of the NDPS
Act.

Section 12(1) and 12(2) of the Anti-Hijacking Act, 2016 contain a
provision similar to Section 45(1) and 45(2) of PMLA, but a provision
similar to Section 44(2) of PMLA is also contained Section 12(3) of
the Anti-Hijacking Act. The aforesaid section reads thus:—
“12. Provision as to bail.—(1) Notwithstanding anything
contained in the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (2 of 1974), no
person accused of an offence punishable under this Act shall, if
in custody, be released on bail or on his own bond, unless,—
(a) the Public Prosecutor has been given an opportunity to
oppose the application for such release; and
(b) where Public Prosecutor opposes the application, the
Designated Court is satisfied that there are reasonable grounds
for believing that he is not guilty of such offence and that he is
not likely to commit any offence while on bail.
(2) The limitations on granting of bail as specified in sub-section
(1) are in addition to the limitation under the Criminal
Page 5 of 21

Procedure Code, 1973 (2 of 1974), or any other law for the time
being in force, on granting bail.
(3) Nothing contained in this section shall be deemed to affect
the special powers of the High Court regarding bail under
Section 439 of the Criminal Procedure Code, 1973 (2 of
1974).”
(Emphasis added)

title: BAIL No. 201600034732024 — Allahabad High Court, 15 Apr 2024 (Judge: RAJESH SINGH CHAUHAN)

paragraphs.text:
Heard Shri Siddhartha Sinha, learned counsel for the
applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State.

As per learned col for the applicant, the present applicant  has
been falsely implicated in the case as he has not committed any
offence as alleged in the FIR. The applicant is in jail since
15.02.2024 in FIR/Crime No.74 of 2022, under Sections 452,
354, 308, 376, 323, 313 of IPC, Police Station Achalganj,
District Unnao.

Attention has been drawn towards impugned FIR wherein the
date of incident is 04.04.2022, whereas FIR was lodged on
07.04.2022 on the advise of the Advocate. In the aforesaid FIR
there are three accused persons including the present applicant.
More or less similar allegations have been levelled against all
the accused persons but during investigation it is found that one
of the accused persons Ashok was not present on the spot on the
date of incident, therefore, final report has been filed against
him and against such final report no protest petition has been
filed on behalf of complainant/ informant. Further, against
another accused person Gajodhar charge sheet has been filed
only under Section 354 I.P.C.

Learned A.G.A. as well as learned counsel for the
complainant have tried to justify the impugned FIR but could
not dispute the aforesaid submissions of Shri Siddhartha Sinha,
learned counsel for the applicant.

Having heard the arguments of learned counsel for the
parties and having perused the material available on record and
without entering into the merits of the issue, I find that the
present applicant may be granted bail for the reason that the
story and the allegations of the FIR could not be corroborated
with the injury report, the complainant/ informant has changed
the story at the stage of recording statement under Section 164
Cr.P.C., there is no eye-witness account of the incident in
question, though the same allegation has been levelled against
one co-accused Ashok but it was found during investigation that
co-accused Ashok was not present at the place of incident,
therefore, final report has been filed in favour of Ashok and no
protest application has been filed by the complainant and the
fact that during course of investigation the applicant/ petitioner
was granted interim protection by the Division Bench of this
Court.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.
